architecture.mechanism: The 3-arm differential manifold utilizes a witness-ratio guard (τref = |rref(t) − rref,0|/rref,0 > 0.03) to isolate reversible concentration polarization from irreversible biofilm fouling, addressing the structural vulnerability of 2-arm cartridges that cannot distinguish reference-arm contamination from test-arm cleanliness.
architecture.intervention: Implement a 3-arm differential permeate flux and electrical resistance monitor on the SWRO train with a dedicated reference channel and witness-ratio guard to enable automated physical cleaning protocols triggered by fouling signatures, replacing the periodic chemical CIP schedule.
architecture.expected_effect: The system reduces the estimation error in fouling detection from 71.17% to 7.72% and maintains the designed permeate recovery by extending the cleaning interval to align with quarterly targets without using chlorine-based disinfection.
architecture.falsification_test: Introduce 10% partial reference fouling (Scenario NC5) into the reference arm; if the system detects the contamination via the witness-ratio guard and maintains an estimation error below 10% instead of the 71.17% observed in 2-arm systems, the mechanism holds.
